observation: Frozen best Na model NA-E009 config (NaFadeNet+ExtrapGate s=50), 3-split val MAPE 0.1087 ± 0.0085 with Relative Huber (delta 0.15). The BatteryLife paper trains CPMLP with MSE.
primary_hypothesis: Replacing Relative Huber by MSE on the standardised EOL (paper loss) changes val MAPE; Relative Huber is expected to be better on MAPE because it optimises relative error, while MSE favours long-life cells.
question_inherited: How much of the result is due to the main loss rather than the architecture? (user request A6-NA)
unresolved_from_reference: Gate stuck at init; late-prefix MAPE 0.10-0.12 on split 2021 while the extrapolation alone reaches 0.04-0.05 there.
why_this_experiment: User 2026-11-09: put MSE on the best Na model and see how MAPE changes (A6-NA).
modification: NA-E009 config, main_loss = 'mse' (F.mse_loss on the standardised EOL), main_loss_ablation = true; everything else identical.
held_constant_components: NA-E009 model and config, split 42, seed 42, Adam 5e-5, batch 128, max 100 / min 5 epochs, patience 5, checkpoint rule (MAPE tolerance 0.005 + Acc@15), data, masks, zero physics/extra loss. Changed: main loss Relative Huber -> MSE.
controlled_variables: Split 42 and training seed 42, minimum 5 / maximum 100 epochs, patience 5 after epoch 5, diagnostics every 50 steps.
expected_evidence: Split-42 MAPE/RMSE/Acc@15 vs NA-E010; prefix bands; bias; 3-split mean vs 0.1087 ± 0.0085.
rejection_condition: Diagnostic ablation (A6-NA), judged on the 3-split mean after NA-E031: MSE is reported as WORSE than Relative Huber if its 3-split MAPE exceeds the parent 0.1087 by >= 0.008, BETTER if it is lower by >= 0.008, otherwise TIED. Never promoted without a user decision.
minimum_evidence_requirements: At least five complete epochs; finite MAPE, Acc@15, MAE, and RMSE from one checkpoint; sample and unique-cell counts for every domain; gradient, update, activation, prediction, mask, and compute diagnostics.
required_diagnostics: Epoch learning curve; selected and minimum-MAPE epochs; NaFadeNet block gradients and updates; activation health; prediction spread and bias; prefix, domain, and EOL errors; domain guardrail flags; padding sensitivity; parameters, memory, time, and throughput.
